patches.old:
As I walked with him, I was glad to see such good things. The shepherd said to me, “Go and bring lime and finely crushed pottery, so that I can fill the hollows left by the stones that were removed and put into the building.[a] Everything around the tower must be made level.”

2. I did as he commanded and brought them to him. “Help me,” he said, “and the work will soon be finished.”[b] He filled the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building, then ordered that the area around the tower be swept and made clean.

3. The virgins took brooms and swept. They removed all the refuse from the tower and sprinkled water, and the place became cheerful and most fitting for the tower.

4. The shepherd said to me, “Everything has been cleaned. If the master comes to inspect the tower, he will have nothing to blame us for.”[c] After saying this, he wanted to leave.

5. But I caught hold of his bag and began solemnly to implore him by the Lord to explain everything he had shown me.[d] He said to me, “I must be occupied elsewhere for a little while, then I will explain everything to you. Wait for me here until I return.”

6. I said to him, “Sir, what will I do here by myself?” “You are not by yourself,” he said. “These virgins are with you.” “Then entrust me to them,” I said. The shepherd called them over and said to them, “I entrust this man to you until I return.” Then he left.

7. I was alone with the virgins. They were even more cheerful and friendly toward me, especially the four most glorious among them.

  yaml_path: translation/extra_canonical/shepherd_of_hermas/087.yaml
  text: 'As I walked with him, I was glad to see such good things. The shepherd said to me, “Go and bring
    lime and finely crushed pottery, so that I can fill the hollows left by the stones that were removed
    and put into the building.[a] Everything around the tower must be made level.”


    2. I did as he commanded and brought them to him. “Help me,” he said, “and the work will soon be finished.”[b]
    He filled the hollows left by the stones that had gone into the building, then ordered that the area
    around the tower be swept and made clean.


    3. The virgins took brooms and swept. They removed all the refuse from the tower and sprinkled water,
    and the place became cheerful and most fitting for the tower.


    4. The shepherd said to me, “Everything has been cleaned. If the master comes to inspect the tower,
    he will have nothing to blame us for.”[c] After saying this, he wanted to leave.


    5. But I caught hold of his bag and began solemnly to implore him by the Lord to explain everything
    he had shown me.[d] He said to me, “I must be occupied elsewhere for a little while, then I will explain
    everything to you. Wait for me here until I return.”


    6. I said to him, “Sir, what will I do here by myself?” “You are not by yourself,” he said. “These
    virgins are with you.” “Then entrust me to them,” I said. The shepherd called them over and said to
    them, “I entrust this man to you until I return.” Then he left.


    7. I was alone with the virgins. They were even more cheerful and friendly toward me, especially the
    four most glorious among them.'
